Definition: from G1156; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow:--borrow, lend.
BiblicalUsage: To lend and to borrow is the daily business of neighbours, and Jesus turns it into a test of love: lend, hoping for nothing again, and your reward shall be great. The law already told Israel to lend freely to the poor, and the Sermon on the Mount tells the disciple to give to him that asks and not to turn away the one who would borrow.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lending without return is one of the plainest marks of a child of God. The world lends to get back; the disciple lends because he has already received.
